title: CFA
kicker: Chartered Financial Analyst — a professional credential, not a degree

value.body: A self-study professional programme in investment management run by CFA Institute, a US-based global body. You pass three exams in sequence — Level I, II and III — covering ethics, financial reporting, valuation, portfolio management and related topics. It is not an Indian university degree; it is recognised by employers in investment research, asset management and related finance work.

items.label: Structure
items.note: Computer-based exams held in set windows through the year; candidates commonly take a few years to finish

items.label: Level I pass rate
items.note: Level II ~45%, Level III ~51%; worldwide, not India-specific

items.label: Level I exam fee
items.note: Early vs standard registration; the one-time US$350 enrolment fee was dropped from April 2025

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register directly with CFA Institute for Level I if you hold a bachelor's degree, are a final-year student within the permitted window before graduation, or have enough qualifying work experience. A valid passport is required. The charter is awarded after passing all three levels plus about 4,000 hours (spread over at least 36 months) of relevant work experience and joining CFA Institute as a member.

value.title: At a glance
items: Fees are in US dollars and are paid per exam attempt, separate from any coaching costs.
Fewer than half of candidates pass Level I in a typical window, so repeat attempts are common; preparation usually runs alongside a degree or job.
Passing the exams alone does not make you a charterholder — the work-experience requirement must also be met.
It is often taken together with a B.Com, M.Com, MBA (Finance) or a finance job, rather than instead of one.
